title: Focus-batch 30-day experiment log — personal KPIs
body:
Context:
I keep getting pulled into small meetings and async threads, and my PR queue sits at 6–10 open PRs for >48 hours. This is a personal experiment to reclaim deep work time and move concrete outputs (PRs merged, design decisions made) while keeping collaboration overhead low.

Objective (30 days):
- Increase merged PRs from 3/week -> >=6/week (small, unblock PRs and finish one larger task).
- Reduce average PR cycle time from 38h -> <=18h.
- Reduce calendar meeting hours by 25% (baseline: ~15 hrs/week -> target: ~11 hrs/week).

Hypothesis:
If I schedule 4 "focus-batch" blocks per week (2x 90m blocks on Tue/Thu mornings + 2x 60m blocks Mon/Fri afternoons) and enforce no-meeting/notifications during those windows, then context switches drop and I ship more small, reviewable artifacts.

Experiment design:
- Duration: 30 days (Feb 5 — Mar 6).
- Focus-batches per week: 4 (Tues/Thu 09:00–10:30, Mon/Fri 15:00–16:00).
- Rules: mute Slack & email notifications during blocks, update status on Slack before/after batch, keep batches public on my calendar as "focus-batch (heads-down)" to signal to teammates.
- Triage slot: daily 30m at 11:30 to unblock urgent items (keeps meetings low).
- Async update: short daily note in #eng-personal-status channel: 2 lines — what I shipped & blocker.

Metrics (how I'll measure):
- merged_prs_weekly: measured by GitHub PRs with label "ship-small" merged by me each week (baseline week of Jan 26–Feb 1 = 3).
- avg_pr_cycle_hours: avg hours from PR opened -> merged for PRs assigned to me (baseline ~38).
- meeting_hours_week: sum of events >15m on calendar (baseline ~15).
- focus_satisfaction: subjective 1–5 at week's end (captures cognitive load).

Baseline snapshot (week before experiment):
- merged_prs_weekly = 3
- avg_pr_cycle_hours = 38
- meeting_hours_week = 15.5
- focus_satisfaction = 2

Weekly check-in template (fill each Friday):
- week_range: YYYY-MM-DD — YYYY-MM-DD
- merged_prs: n
- avg_cycle_hours: n.h
- meeting_hours: n.h
- focus_blocks_done: x/4
- blockers: short list
- experiments/notes: quick notes, e.g., "shifted Tue block to 10:00, reduced meeting invites"

Day-to-day micro-rules (to keep this pragmatic):
- Keep PRs <= 300 lines of changes where possible.
- Prefer 1–2 small, focused commits per PR.
- Use draft PRs early to gather synchronous feedback only in narrow cases.
- If a meeting is requested during a focus-block, propose immediate alternatives: triage slot or same-day async update.

Example week log (filled in as template):
- week_range: 2026-02-09 — 2026-02-15
- merged_prs: 5
- avg_cycle_hours: 22.4
- meeting_hours: 12.5
- focus_blocks_done: 3/4 (missed Fri afternoon)
- blockers: waiting on infra review for quantization test harness (LIN-2345)
- experiments/notes: "Daily 11:30 triage worked well — cleared 4 small unblockers. Had to push one block due to customer call."

Retrospective prompts (end of 30 days):
- Did merged_prs_weekly increase sustainably? By how much?
- What caused reductions in PR cycle time — faster reviews, smaller PRs, or fewer context switches?
- Which calendar/meeting types are safe to keep/reduce?
- What social friction occurred when blocking time on my calendar? Any perception issues?
- Next iteration: scale to 6 focus-batches/week? Move to different times?

Notes to self / quick checklist:
- Before batch: set status to "heads-down", add one-line goal in the calendar event.
- After batch: push a short update to #eng-personal-status and tag reviewers if PRs ready.
- Weekly: export PR stats from GitHub (use saved search: is:pr author:@mikael is:merged label:ship-small merged:>=2026-02-05).

Potential risks / mitigations:
- Risk: teammates feel blocked -> Mitigation: publish triage window + allow urgent invites with clear subject prefix "URGENT".
- Risk: meetings shift to other people’s calendars and create synchronous pressure -> Mitigation: keep an "office hours" 1x/week slot for collaboration.

Next steps (short):
- Feb 4: finalize calendar blocks and set default "focus-batch" visibility.
- Feb 5: start experiment.
- Feb 12, Feb 19, Feb 26: quick Friday retros.
- Mar 6: final 30-day retrospective and decide next iteration.

Misc notes / free-form thoughts:
- If this reduces context switches, could be a simple pattern to share as a team culture idea (brown-bag + template calendar event).
- Consider pairing one batch/week with a reviewer (hard stop after 60m) to accelerate merges for infra-dependent PRs.
- Remember to track energy as well as output — when I am doing back-to-back deep work my ability to review late in day drops.

Done/Outcomes (to update as I go):
- [ ] baseline recorded
- [ ] calendar blocks published
- [ ] first-week log entered
- [ ] share short summary with manager after 2 weeks

End of doc.
